method: Development probe of the interactive walkthrough. Real Claude Code, Cortex capture, Evolve consistency learning, reviewed copy, MCP retrieval, and first-request injection. Probe launches used bounded -p automation; the walkthrough launches interactive Claude Code with normal permissions.
task:
What focal length was used to take sample.jpg? Use embedded EXIF metadata.
Report both the actual focal length in mm and the 35 mm equivalent if present,
and name the EXIF tags supporting each value. Preserve the stored numeric
precision rather than rounding a formatted display value. Use local tools. If you use Python,
run it with uv run --no-sync --project "$DEMO_EVOLVE_REPO" python.
Save the extracted metadata as photo-result.json using the tool's native
EXIF tag names and numeric values. In your answer, identify which tag is
actual focal length and which is the equivalent. Report missing tags as
missing rather than guessing. Do not install packages.

training.task:
Where was sample.jpg taken? Use embedded EXIF metadata and local tools.
Show the raw GPS latitude/longitude values and their N/S/E/W references,
then convert them to signed decimal coordinates. State what the metadata
supports about the location. If you use Python, run it with
uv run --no-sync --project "$DEMO_EVOLVE_REPO" python.
Do not install packages. Show the successful extraction command so the
procedure can be repeated with other photos.
training.learned_guideline: When extracting GPS coordinates for machine processing, use extraction tool flags that output numeric, machine-readable formats (such as exiftool's -n and -j options) and save results directly to a file.
training.rationale: Machine-readable extraction prevents errors from manual parsing or rounding, ensures precision is preserved, and enables reliable downstream automation across varying EXIF metadata.

promoted.content: When extracting GPS coordinates for machine processing, use extraction tool flags that output numeric, machine-readable formats (such as exiftool's -n and -j options) and save results directly to a file.

baseline.final_answer:
Here are the focal length details extracted from sample.jpg using native EXIF tag names and numeric values:

- Actual focal length (EXIF tag FocalLength): 4.4 mm
- 35 mm equivalent focal length (EXIF tag FocalLengthIn35mmFormat): 27 mm

Supporting tags:
- FocalLength: "4.4 mm" (this is the actual lens focal length in millimeters)
- FocalLengthIn35mmFormat: "27 mm" (this is the equivalent focal length for a 35mm camera system)

Both tags are present and were not computed or guessed—they are directly from the EXIF metadata.

The extracted metadata is saved as photo-result.json using the native EXIF tag names. No values are rounded; the precision is as stored in the metadata.

If you need to review the raw JSON or any more tags, let me know!

Native-memory/config directories, conversations, and photo output folders were fresh per arm; identical source image and installed tools. Only the GPS training session was ingested into this serving namespace.
